sections.content: When most investors think about affordable real estate markets in the South, they picture Memphis or Birmingham. But Shreveport, Louisiana deserves a serious look. With median home prices well below the national average, a stable tenant base, and a steady supply of distressed properties, Shreveport offers real estate deals that are hard to find in more competitive markets. Whether you are a first-time investor just getting started — check out this [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide — or a seasoned wholesaler looking for your next market, Shreveport has something to offer.
Shreveport LA Market Overview: What Investors Need to Know

Shreveport is Louisiana's third-largest city, sitting in the northwest corner of the state near the Texas and Arkansas borders. The city has a population of roughly 185,000 and serves as a regional hub for healthcare, education, and energy. Major employers include Ochsner LSU Health, Barksdale Air Force Base, and a growing film production industry — Louisiana's generous tax incentives have made it a popular destination for Hollywood productions. These anchors create a consistent pool of renters and buyers, which matters a great deal when you are evaluating long-term investment potential.

The Shreveport metro area has seen modest but steady population growth driven largely by military personnel at Barksdale and healthcare workers. Vacancy rates for single-family rentals have hovered around 8 to 10 percent, which is healthy for a market of this size. Property taxes in Caddo Parish are relatively low, and Louisiana's homestead exemption reduces assessed values for owner-occupants, keeping overall holding costs manageable for investors.
Average Home Prices in Shreveport

One of the biggest draws for investors is Shreveport's affordability. As of late 2024, the median home price in Shreveport sits around $145,000 to $160,000, compared to the national median of roughly $415,000. Distressed properties — the bread and butter of wholesalers and flippers — can often be acquired in the $40,000 to $90,000 range, with after-repair values (ARVs) in stable neighborhoods landing between $120,000 and $200,000. That spread creates real profit potential for investors who know how to run their numbers. Use our free [ARV Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator) to quickly estimate after-repair value before you make an offer.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Shreveport

Not every zip code in Shreveport is created equal. Like any city, some areas carry higher risk, and others punch well above their weight for investors. Here is a breakdown of neighborhoods worth your attention.
South Shreveport

South Shreveport is the market's most stable submarket. Home values are higher here — typically $170,000 to $280,000 — but so is demand. Buyers and renters in this area tend to be professionals and military families, which means lower turnover and easier tenant screening. Flips do well here because buyers are plentiful and mortgage-ready. If you are running a buy-and-hold strategy, South Shreveport offers more predictable cash flow.
Broadmoor and Queensborough

These mid-city neighborhoods offer some of the best wholesale and flip opportunities in the metro. Properties are older — mostly 1940s through 1970s construction — and many are owned free and clear by long-time residents or heirs. That means more motivated sellers and better chances of finding off-market deals. ARVs typically range from $110,000 to $160,000, and acquisition prices on distressed homes can be as low as $30,000 to $60,000.
Bossier City

Technically a separate city across the Red River, Bossier City is part of the Shreveport metro and should not be overlooked. With Barksdale Air Force Base nearby, there is constant rental demand from military families on short-term assignments. Median prices run slightly higher than Shreveport proper, but the tenant base is arguably more reliable. Duplexes and small multifamily properties in Bossier City are particularly attractive for landlords.

Pro Tip: When evaluating neighborhoods in Shreveport, cross-reference crime data from the Shreveport Police Department's public map with school ratings on GreatSchools.org. Investors often overlook this combination, but it is one of the fastest ways to separate neighborhoods with long-term appreciation potential from those that will be a headache to manage.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Shreveport
Wholesale Deals

Shreveport is a wholesaler-friendly market. There is a solid inventory of distressed, vacant, and probate properties in neighborhoods like Queensborough, Cedar Grove, and Allendale. These areas have higher rates of delinquent taxes and absentee ownership, which translates directly into motivated sellers willing to accept below-market offers. If you are new to the strategy, start with our guide on [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) to understand how to structure deals correctly before approaching sellers.
Fix and Flip Opportunities

Fix and flip deals in Shreveport work best in transitional neighborhoods close to employment centers or hospitals. The key is keeping renovation budgets tight — Shreveport buyers are price-sensitive, and you cannot over-improve a home in a $140,000 neighborhood and expect to sell it for $200,000. Cosmetic flips — new flooring, paint, fixtures, and landscaping — often generate the best returns here. Aim for a total all-in cost (purchase plus rehab plus carrying costs) of no more than 70 percent of ARV. Run your numbers with our free [Wholesale Deal Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator) before you commit to a project.
Buy and Hold Rentals

Rental demand in Shreveport is driven by a large renter population — approximately 48 percent of Shreveport households rent rather than own, which is well above the national average. Single-family homes in the $80,000 to $120,000 purchase range can often be rented for $950 to $1,250 per month, producing cap rates between 8 and 12 percent when managed properly. Section 8 voucher holders represent a significant portion of the rental market, and many investors find that HUD-assisted rentals provide reliable, on-time payments that offset the lower-income area risks.
Local Market Trends Investors Should Watch

items: Film industry growth: Louisiana's entertainment tax credits continue attracting productions to Shreveport, creating short-term rental demand and increased foot traffic to local businesses.
Healthcare expansion: Ochsner Health's ongoing investment in the region is adding jobs and increasing demand for housing near medical corridors.
Rising insurance costs: Louisiana property insurance rates have climbed sharply statewide. Budget 1.5 to 2 percent of property value annually for insurance when underwriting Shreveport deals.
Infrastructure investment: The City of Shreveport has committed to street and sewer improvements in several older neighborhoods, which tends to precede modest appreciation in surrounding home values.
Tight lending environment: Many buyers in Shreveport's lower price ranges face financing hurdles, which keeps demand high for affordable rentals and seller-financed transactions.

Practical Tips for Out-of-State Investors Eyeing Shreveport

Shreveport is increasingly attracting out-of-state capital, particularly from California, New York, and Texas investors priced out of their home markets. If you are considering investing remotely, here is how to approach it the right way.

items: Build a local team first: Find a property manager, a real estate attorney familiar with Louisiana law, and a reliable contractor before you close your first deal. Louisiana has unique legal quirks, including its civil law heritage, that can catch out-of-state investors off guard.

Visit in person at least once: Shreveport neighborhoods can look similar on a map but feel very different on the ground. A single trip to walk streets, visit properties, and meet your team in person will save you from expensive mistakes.

Focus on off-market properties: The best deals in Shreveport rarely hit the MLS at attractive prices. Learning [how to find off-market real estate deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals) through direct mail, driving for dollars, and probate leads will give you a serious edge over investors relying only on listed inventory.

Understand flood zone risk: Parts of Shreveport sit in FEMA flood zones, and flood insurance can add $1,500 to $3,000 or more to your annual holding costs. Always check FEMA flood maps before making an offer.

Analyze deals conservatively: Use realistic vacancy rates of 10 to 12 percent and budget for deferred maintenance. Shreveport's older housing stock often has hidden costs. Learning [how to analyze real estate deals like a pro](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/how-to-analyze-real-estate-deals) will help you stress-test your numbers before you are committed.

sections.content: Pro Tip: Louisiana uses a unique property ownership system called the Succession process (similar to probate in other states). Many Shreveport properties are tied up in succession because heirs have not formalized ownership after a family member's death. These 'heir properties' are often prime off-market opportunities — but always work with a local real estate attorney to ensure clear title before closing.

Is Shreveport Right for Your Investment Strategy?

Shreveport is not a glamorous market, and that is precisely the point. Glamorous markets are expensive, competitive, and unforgiving of mistakes. Shreveport rewards investors who do their homework, build the right local network, and approach deals with disciplined underwriting. The combination of low acquisition costs, strong rental demand, and consistent deal flow makes it a market worth serious consideration — whether you are looking to wholesale your first contract or build a portfolio of cash-flowing rentals.
